hints: Focus on the vapour as an ideal gas, so start from $pV = nRT$ and remember that moles links mass to $M_r$.
Write moles as $n = m / M_r$ with $m = 0.10\text{ g}$, then rearrange to make $M_r$ the subject.
Check your units carefully, $p$ must be in Pa and $V$ must be in $\text{m}^3$, so convert $85\text{ cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$ before substituting.
walkthrough:
**Link mass to moles with the ideal gas equation**

Think of the evaporated liquid as a gas filling the extra syringe volume. Moles and $M_r$ are linked by $n = m / M_r$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$pV = nRT \text{ and } n = \frac{m}{M_r}$$

**Rearrange to make $M_r$ the subject**

Substitute for $n$ to get $pV = (m / M_r)RT$, then rearrange. This puts mass and $RT$ on top and $pV$ underneath.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$M_r = \frac{mRT}{pV}$$

**Insert values with correct SI units**

Use $m = 0.10\text{ g}$, $R = 8.31$, $T = 400\text{ K}$, $p = 101300\text{ Pa}$. Volume must be in $\text{m}^3$, and $1\text{ cm}^3 = 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$V = 85 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$$
$$M_r = (0.10 \times 8.31 \times 400) \div (85 \times 10^{-6} \times 101300)$$

options.A: This is upside down. It calculates $(pV) \div (mRT)$ which is $1 / M_r$, not $M_r$. It also forgets to convert $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.
options.B: This is also upside down, giving $1 / M_r$. It also mixes units by using $101.3$ instead of $101300\text{ Pa}$ while keeping $R = 8.31$ which needs Pa and $\text{m}^3$.
options.C: This correctly uses $M_r = mRT / pV$ with all SI units. Mass is $0.10$, $RT$ is $8.31 \times 400$, pressure is $101300\text{ Pa}$ and volume is correctly converted as $85 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$.
options.D: The rearrangement and volume conversion are correct, but pressure is wrong. Using $101.3$ means kPa, which does not match $R = 8.31$ in Pa $\text{m}^3$ units. You must use $101300$.
